meta.title: Destinations: where can you study with A-Levels?
meta.description: UK, USA, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Canada: A-Level admission routes for students from Uzbekistan.

header.title: Where can A-Levels take you?
header.lede: Every country has its own admission route. Below is the general picture for a student from Uzbekistan; exact requirements are updated every year.

meta.title: United Kingdom: an undergraduate degree with A-Levels, no foundation year
meta.description: With an Uzbek school certificate most UK universities require a foundation year. With A-Levels you apply through UCAS straight to an undergraduate degree.

header.title: United Kingdom
header.lede: With A-Levels you save a year and a year of living costs in the UK.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: School certificate only
rows.value: Most universities require a one-year foundation first (for example: Edinburgh, Cardiff, Nottingham).

rows.label: With A-Levels
rows.value: You can apply directly to the first year without a foundation year (for example: Queen Mary, Liverpool).

rows.label: Application
rows.value: Through UCAS.

rows.label: Medicine
rows.value: UCAT is required.

blocks.title: Language requirements
paragraphs: Most universities ask for IELTS or an equivalent English certificate. The score you need depends on the subject.

items.q: Can I go straight to a UK university with my school certificate?
items.a: Most universities require a foundation year first. With A-Levels you can apply to an undergraduate degree without one.

items.q: How many A-Levels do I need?
items.a: Usually three. The university and subject decide which subjects and grades are needed.
UCAS deadlines vary by university and subject; we plan your exams around them.

items.title: Queen Mary University of London: Uzbekistan

meta.title: USA: a strong application with SAT and A-Levels
meta.description: You can apply to US universities with a school certificate; most selective universities require SAT/ACT again. A-Levels strengthen your application.

header.title: USA
header.lede: SAT plus A-Levels: a strong combination for your US application.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: School certificate
rows.value: You can apply with your school certificate. Most selective universities have made SAT/ACT required again.

rows.label: With A-Levels
rows.value: Strengthens your application academically. Some universities accept A-Level results from international applicants as an alternative.

rows.label: Application
rows.value: Through Common App; scholarship research matters.

items.a: As a general rule, no. Some universities make exceptions, so we check each university's policy separately.
Scholarships depend on the university and the family's financial situation. Scholarship research is part of our application service.

items.q: Do I need an English certificate?
items.a: Most universities ask for TOEFL or IELTS.

items.title: SAT/ACT policies at selective colleges, 2026–27 (summary source; checked against official pages)

meta.title: Germany: an A-Level route without a Studienkolleg
meta.description: Three A-Levels at grade C or above (two from the 'A list') give direct access to higher education in Germany. Pearson IAL is assessed under the same rules.

header.title: Germany
header.lede: With the right subject choice, an undergraduate degree in Germany without a Studienkolleg.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: School certificate only
rows.value: Usually requires a Studienkolleg first (1 year, in German) or prior study at a university in Uzbekistan.

rows.label: With A-Levels
rows.value: Three A-Levels at grade C or above (two from 'A list' subjects such as languages, maths, sciences or economics) give direct access to higher education.

rows.label: Medicine
rows.value: All 3 subjects must come from the maths and science group.

rows.label: Pearson IAL
rows.value: Assessed under the same rules.

rows.label: Final decision
rows.value: Made by the recognition body (uni-assist / ZAB). That is why subjects must be chosen correctly from the start.

items.q: Do I need to speak German?
items.a: For German-taught programmes, yes. There are also English-taught programmes; language requirements depend on the programme.

items.q: Which subjects are on the 'A list'?
items.a: Languages, maths, sciences, economics and similar subjects. We check the exact combination for your degree with you.

items.q: Is a Studienkolleg definitely not needed?
items.a: If the conditions are met, no. The final decision rests with the recognition body.

items.title: Pearson: Germany relaxes admission requirements for UK qualifications

meta.title: Italy: the 12-year requirement and the A-Level solution
meta.description: Undergraduate study in Italy requires at least 12 years of schooling; school in Uzbekistan lasts 11 years. Three different A-Levels are one way to meet the requirement. IMAT is also available.

header.title: Italy
header.lede: Complete your 11 years of school with A-Levels and apply directly to English-taught degrees in Italy.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: Requirement
rows.value: At least 12 years of schooling for an undergraduate degree. School in Uzbekistan lasts 11 years.

rows.label: With A-Levels
rows.value: Three different A-Levels are one of the ways to meet this requirement. Universities may set additional conditions.

rows.label: Medicine
rows.value: IMAT for English-taught medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine (run by the Ministry, late September).

items.q: Do I need a foundation year?
items.a: If three different A-Levels meet the 12-year requirement, you may not need one. We check the university's requirements with you.

items.q: Do I need to speak Italian?

items.a: Usually in late September. Exact dates are announced each year.

meta.title: Netherlands: English-taught degrees with A-Levels
meta.description: English-taught bachelor's programmes are common in the Netherlands. Applications are assessed per programme; A-Levels are a much stronger route than a school certificate.

header.title: Netherlands
header.lede: Apply to English-taught bachelor's programmes with A-Levels.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: Programmes
rows.value: English-taught bachelor's programmes are common.

rows.label: Assessment
rows.value: Applications are assessed per programme; A-Levels are a much stronger route than a school certificate.

rows.label: Requirements
rows.value: We check them with you on the programme's page.

meta.title: Canada: university entry with A-Levels
meta.description: A-Levels are a recognised entry qualification at Canadian universities such as Toronto and McGill. Applications go to the university or through a provincial system.

header.title: Canada
header.lede: Apply to universities such as Toronto and McGill with A-Levels.

blocks.title: The route for a student from Uzbekistan

rows.label: A-Levels
rows.value: A recognised entry qualification at universities such as Toronto and McGill.

rows.label: Application
rows.value: Directly to the university or through a provincial system (for example: OUAC).
